notes: San Francisco Bay Guardian, 2008 to 2010, 210 items in the Internet Archive collection (many issues are there twice, as two scans), read from the DjVu text. Hand-curated: news-word passages, article clusters and event passages were read and each finding's quote checked against the issue. People rule as in the dossier: no owners, staff, tenants, performers or customers.

coverage.note: 210 items; 78,583 numbered-address mentions on EAS streets, of which the advertisement filter marked 66,930 and kept 2,889 windows in 2,165 address clusters. Read in full: the 68 passages of the news-word pass over the raw text, the 59 clusters of article prose, and the 33 event-word passages for places printed without a number. The 236 event-word clusters under the tighter filter were not read. About 20 candidates were checked against the issue text; 16 were written and 1 dropped (the McMillan Drop-in Center at 39 Fell, whose closing the paper does not date). Not entered: five stories about private owners and tenants. 15 findings, each quote found again in the issue's text. 9 resolved and published on 9 existing pages. 4 held as single facts on parcels with no page (55 Laguna, 3422 Mission, 736 Valencia, 1268 Lombard). 2 unresolved because EAS does not have the number: 113 Steuart and 1856 Mission. The yield is far lower than in earlier decades: the paper's building reporting in these years is mostly policy, without addresses. The audit flags 1 of 15, a move the paper dates by an event and not a year.

findings.description: The Little House, a two-storey cottage about 148 years old that stood here, by some accounts one of the ten oldest houses in the city and one of the few on Russian Hill to survive 1906, was demolished on 16 March 2009. It was vacant, and came down on an emergency permit issued with about a week's notice after an engineer for the owners reported it in danger of collapse; preservationists disputed that, and the president of the Board of Supervisors proposed changes to the building code.
